claims.subject: court_life

claims.subject: ceramic
claims.value: Sancai glazed earthenware is a strong Tang ceramic anchor.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Sancai is safer as a strongly recognizable Tang ceramic cue than later mature Jingdezhen blue-and-white porcelain.
prompt_implications: When a generic Tang ceramic prop is needed, prefer period-appropriate glazed earthenware or another specifically evidenced Tang ceramic rather than defaulting to later blue-and-white porcelain.
safer_alternatives: Tang glazed earthenware / sancai where appropriate
plain or period-specific Tang ceramic vessel

claims.subject: ceramic_decoration
claims.value: Cobalt decoration and Tang blue-and-white experiments existed, but they do not justify treating the later mature Jingdezhen blue-and-white porcelain tradition as standard Tang material culture.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Distinguish early/rare Tang cobalt-decorated wares from the later Yuan/Ming blue-and-white porcelain system.
prompt_implications: If blue/cobalt decoration is retained in a Tang scene, make it a narrowly evidenced, exceptional Tang ceramic interpretation—not a familiar Ming-style blue-and-white vase.
safer_alternatives: narrowly evidenced Tang cobalt-decorated ceramic with uncertainty noted

strict_reconstruction.instruction: Do not render a mature Jingdezhen-style blue-and-white porcelain vase. Replace it with a strongly evidenced Tang ceramic, or use a narrowly evidenced Tang cobalt-decorated ware only if the case is explicitly framed as exceptional and uncertain.

historically_informed.instruction: Preserve the user’s blue-and-white intent only as a restrained Tang cobalt-decorated ceramic interpretation; avoid later standardized Yuan/Ming shapes and decoration.

period_drama.instruction: A familiar blue-and-white visual convention may be used for readability, but mark it internally as a later-inspired period-drama adaptation rather than documentary Tang evidence.

fantasy_hybrid.instruction: Allow the blue-and-white porcelain deliberately as a fantasy/hybrid object and do not describe it as historically authentic Tang material culture.

claims.subject: ceramic_chronology
claims.value: Mature underglaze-cobalt blue-and-white porcelain became a major Jingdezhen development in the Yuan/fourteenth-century context and flourished later.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: This claim is specifically about importing the mature later blue-and-white porcelain visual system into Tang reconstruction.
prompt_implications: Avoid familiar Yuan/Ming Jingdezhen blue-and-white porcelain motifs, vessel profiles, and production finish in strict Tang reconstruction.
safer_alternatives: exceptional Tang cobalt-decorated ware with uncertainty

strict_reconstruction.instruction: Replace mature later blue-and-white porcelain with a period-compatible Tang ceramic solution.

historically_informed.instruction: Translate the color idea into an exceptional Tang cobalt-decorated ceramic while avoiding later Jingdezhen conventions.

period_drama.instruction: Permit mature later-style blue-and-white only as an explicit later-inspired cinematic convention, not as documentary Tang evidence.

fantasy_hybrid.instruction: Permit mature later-style blue-and-white as an intentional cross-period hybrid, not as historically authentic Tang material culture.
